item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' arrives with enormous hype and expectations after 13-year wait
item.description: After a 13-year wait, one of entertainment's biggest releases is finally here.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump plans to meet separately with Putin on his China trip in addition to their 3-way talks with Xi
item.description: President Donald Trump plans to meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a U.S. official confirmed.

item.title: NPR: Veteran reporter asks SCOTUS to hear case on protecting confidential sources
item.description: A longtime national security reporter is facing steep fines in a civil lawsuit for failing to disclose her source. She's asking the Supreme Court to weigh in.

item.title: NPR: Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House
item.description: The New York Democrat moved a step closer to becoming the first Black lawmaker in U.S. history to serve in the job, after House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support him.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to become House speaker, a historic first
item.description: Jeffries brushed past skeptics and was on track to make history as the nation's first Black American with the gavel.

item.title: NPR: House Democrat warns 13 Trump allies to save their records for upcoming investigations
item.description: Among the recipients of letters from Robert Garcia, incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, are Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, Jared Kushner and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: DHS Secretary Mullin testifies on worldwide threats amid tech outages, Iran warnings
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is set to appear Wednesday at a congressional hearing about threats facing the country at a time of looming questions over cyber infrastructure, the future of immigration enforcement and his decision to fly to the LSU-Texas college football game as travelers across the U.S. were still stuck at airports after the nationwide grounding of flights.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat, beating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan
item.description: The Alaska race was the last U.S. Senate contest to be resolved in this year's midterm elections and gave Democrats a 56-44 majority after they flipped nine GOP-held seats to retake the chamber.

item.title: NPR: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.

item.title: NPR: Mary Peltola flips Alaska's Senate seat. And, Nvidia won't reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has won one of the U.S.' most watched Senate races. And, Nvidia's board says it doesn't plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang despite pressure from his allies.

item.title: NPR: Trump lands in China with key meetings with Xi and Putin on the agenda
item.description: Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's visit to Washington in September.

item.title: NPR: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.

item.title: NPR: Project Gryffindor: Meta's plan to get more school kids using Instagram
item.description: Meta said it launched its "school partnership program" to keep teens safe, but internal documents tell a different story.

item.title: NPR: She retired early to care for family. New work rules for food aid disrupted that
item.description: The Trump administration's sweeping changes to SNAP food aid mean older adults up to age 65 must work or volunteer to get the benefit.

item.title: NPR: Mary Peltola flips Alaska's Senate seat into Democrats' column
item.description: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has narrowly won Alaska's U.S. Senate race, toppling the Republican incumbent, according to a race call by The Associated Press.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What a string of tech problems reveals about America's digital vulnerabilities
item.description: A string of major technology failures is raising new questions about the reliability and security of systems millions of Americans depend on every day. The incidents are said to be unrelated, but their timing has fueled concerns about whether something more is at work. Geoff Bennett discussed the wave of disruptions with Eric O'Neill, a former FBI counterintelligence operative.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A look at China's technology industry amid AI race with the U.S.
item.description: President Trump began a 48-hour visit to Asia with a summit of regional countries in the Philippines. On Wednesday, the president heads to China for meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. One of the key pressure points between the U.S. and China is technology and the AI race. Nick Schifrin is in China and visited one of its largest technology companies.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What's in Trump's $50 billion air traffic control overhaul plan
item.description: The Trump administration is seeking $50 billion to modernize the nation's air traffic control system following last week's massive nationwide ground stop. But the proposal could face resistance in Congress, where lawmakers are raising questions about the cost and how the money would be spent. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins breaks down the price tag and the political hurdles ahead.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Biden releases memoir recounting his presidency and decision to drop out in 2024
item.description: Almost two years after leaving office, former President Joe Biden has penned a memoir about his time in the White House. "Promise Me, America," is out, but Biden isn't out doing the typical run of media interviews. Amna Nawaz discussed more with his former counselor, Steve Ricchetti.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Study reveals energy demands and emissions of America's data centers
item.description: The 400 largest data centers in the United States emit more greenhouse gas emissions in one year than the entire nation of Denmark, according to a new report from Harvard University. From May 2024 to April 2025, data centers accounted for nearly 2% of total U.S. energy consumption and produced more than 25 million metric tons of CO2. Amna Nawaz spoke with the study's lead author, Gianluca Guidi.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: North Dakota museum gives Great Plains artists a bigger stage
item.description: The North Dakota Museum of Art in Grand Forks is bringing great art to the Great Plains. It's also supporting artists in a region where gaining visibility and a market can be tough. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown visited for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What a 194-year-old tortoise could teach humans about living longer
item.description: What secrets might a 194-year-old tortoise have for humans when it comes to living longer? William Brangham examines the remarkable life of Jonathan.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: U.S. no longer considered a measles-free nation
item.description: In our news wrap Tuesday, international health officials say the United States is no longer considered a measles-free nation, a Harvard study shows cellphone bans in some schools are leading to modest improvements in academic growth among students and maritime monitors say a gas tanker went up in flames in the Strait of Hormuz after it was hit by multiple projectiles.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: China and Canada expand tariff relief while relations with the U.S. are strained
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney both praised the strategic partnership they agreed to pursue this year and pointed to improving economic ties.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Doctors are raising concerns about U.S. babies born with measles
item.description: Congenital measles happens when a pregnant woman passes the virus to her fetus in the womb and can lead to serious complications or even be deadly for newborns.
item.category: centers for disease control and prevention

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia chair says board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: The announcement followed Huang's statement earlier in the day that he would come back to lead the chipmaker if the board invited him.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Apple joins the list of recent tech breakdowns after an update goes awry
item.description: Apple acknowledged on its system status page that its Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare services suffered full outages.

item.title: NPR: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
item.description: Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America , goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how our approach to criminals has changed over time.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Can the U.S. regain its measles elimination status? Here's what to know
item.description: The U.S. has lost its measles-elimination status for the first time in 26 years, an international health organization determined Tuesday.

item.title: NPR: How often lawmakers miss congressional votes — and why it matters
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with Eric Schickler, UC Berkeley political science professor, about voting absenteeism on Capitol Hill, and how commonplace it is for lawmakers to miss votes.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ex-CEO Jensen Huang signals interest in returning to Nvidia after resigning amid scandal
item.description: He resigned last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip with economic deals and talks with allies
item.description: President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, where he met with regional partners, sought to formalize a trade deal and get a break from a series of setbacks at home, ranging from a major disruption to the U.S. aviation industry to a scandal that has shaken the global AI industry.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The long wait is almost over. Here's what to know about the upcoming release of 'Grand Theft Auto VI'
item.description: After a 13-year wait since its last main installment, "Grand Theft Auto VI" is preparing for another big score.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 400 largest U.S. data centers produced more carbon dioxide in a year than Denmark, study finds
item.description: Researchers estimated electricity use by the centers produced around 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide, according to a study in Monday's Nature Sustainability.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Van Hollen's bid to replace Schumer puts pressure on Democrats to take sides
item.description: The Dec. 1 contest has put Senate Democrats on edge and has forced what could become an ugly public fight immediately after major victories in the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'The symbol of the occupation': Ukraine destroys span of Kerch Bridge linking Russia with Crimea
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy portrayed the bridge operation as a masterstroke following a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration details its $50 billion request for aviation system improvements
item.description: The Trump administration has formally updated its request to lawmakers for $50.1 billion to modernize the nation's air traffic control system and to make other improvements at airports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FAA stops installation of routers it linked to national ground stop
item.description: The decision was made after technicians linked Friday's disruption of key air traffic control systems to one of these routers that had just been installed in El Dorado, Arkansas.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mullin defends use of government plane to attend football game after ground stop
item.description: Mullin's flight took place after the stoppage was lifted and as flights were back in the air. But thousands of flights were canceled because of the ground stop, and Mullin flew as people nationwide were forced to scramble for alternative travel options.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iran fires at U.S. facility in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on Arab neighbors
item.description: The move on Tuesday was Iran's third attack on American military targets in the kingdom in recent days as Tehran resumed strikes on its Arab neighbors after a two-month lull.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Retail spending slowed in October as high prices gave shoppers pause
item.description: Shoppers increased spending more slowly in October as economic uncertainty and high prices led more Americans to pull back on a variety of purchases.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Debunking social media posts that claim a 90-day blackout will start Nov. 17
item.description: Americans don't need to stockpile for widespread disruptions to power, water and food supplies, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

item.title: NPR: Huang says he'd be "honored" to return to Nvidia as he agrees to testify to Congress
item.description: The former Nvidia CEO's comments come as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly amid a swirl of national security scandals.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. and Mexico officially lose measles elimination status
item.description: The U.S. has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread — largely among the unvaccinated — at the highest rate in more than 30 years.
item.category: centers for disease control and prevention

item.title: NPR: Sen. Jack Reed says FAA needs a real plan, not just more money
item.description: Sen. Jack Reed raised concerns about FAA oversight of contractors after last week's nationwide ground stop and criticized the Trump administration's request for $50 billion in additional funding.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing for Hung Cao as Navy secretary
item.description: The Senate Armed Services Committee is holding a confirmation hearing Tuesday to consider the nomination of acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao as he seeks to permanently take over as the top civilian official.

item.title: NPR: Trump is in Asia ahead of Xi, Putin summit. And, tech leaders want Huang back at Nvidia
item.description: Trump says he plans to discuss Ukraine during his Asia trip, which contradicts what the White House previously announced. And, Silicon Valley leaders are pushing for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia.

item.title: NPR: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
item.description: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

item.title: NPR: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
item.description: Manila is President Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: NPR: After Democrats' midterm wins, some hope attacks on DEI will ease
item.description: After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. What does Democrats' ascendance portend for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration has relentlessly attacked?

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why many white South Africans who left are migrating back home
item.description: President Trump has alleged that violence in South Africa has targeted the country's white minority. While his administration has had a strict ban on refugee admissions, it has carved out an exception for white South Africans. Of the over 16,000 refugees admitted through September, all but five were from South Africa. But as Fred de Sam Lazaro reports, that migration is becoming a two-way trend.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump appeals to state and federal courts to erase hush money criminal conviction
item.description: A federal appeals court is weighing whether it can — or should — intervene in President Donald Trump's hush money case now that a New York State appellate court has heard arguments in his quest to erase the historic conviction.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge sets March retrial date for Lindsay Clancy in deaths of her 3 children
item.description: A Massachusetts judge on Monday scheduled Lindsay Clancy's retrial for late March after prosecutors signaled that — at least for now — they intend to prosecute her again on first-degree murder charges in the killings of her three young children.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New documentary explores history of crime and punishment in America
item.description: A new PBS documentary, "Crime and Punishment in America," traces the evolution of policing, prisons and the criminal justice system across four centuries. Directed by Lynn Novick and executive produced by Ken Burns, the series examines how Americans have defined crime, determined punishment and wrestled with questions about justice and fairness. Novick joined Geoff Bennett to discuss the film.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope bids 'hasta luego' to Peru as he wraps up marathon South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo XIV bid farewell to his beloved second homeland of Peru on Monday with an "hasta luego," after a marathon 12-day South American tour that tested his stamina after lung cancer surgery.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration seeks to deflect responsibility for nationwide ground stop
item.description: Three days after air travel was halted in the longest nationwide ground stop since 9/11, the focus has turned to how the air traffic control network can be fixed. The Trump administration is calling for tens of billions of dollars to pay for improvements, but Democrats are questioning that price tag, saying billions have already been approved for an FAA overhaul. Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What went wrong with air traffic control and will more FAA funding fix it?
item.description: To discuss what went wrong to cause Friday's nationwide ground stop, and the funding fight that is brewing in Washington, Amna Nawaz sat down with aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien and congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Trump departs for trip to Asia, meetings with Xi and Putin
item.description: In our news wrap Monday, President Trump left for Asia, where he'll meet regional leaders, followed by talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that North Korea is providing Russia with ballistic missiles and customers at some of the country's largest banks reported difficulty accessing their accounts online.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. works to close loophole that let China access advanced AI chips
item.description: The Trump administration announced new rules today to further restrict China's access to advanced chips for the use of AI. It comes as questions are mounting about how the Commerce Department allowed loopholes for chip exports. The rule puts new restrictions on overseas data centers and is designed to counter possible smuggling. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Liza Tobin.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: United Airlines says it resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights
item.description: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on Trump's summit with Xi and Putin
item.description: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Geoff Bennett to discuss the latest political news, including President Trump's trip to Asia, his planned meetings with the leaders of China and Russia, what the summit might accomplish, Trump blaming Biden for the FAA's problems and the battle over Democratic leadership in Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump backs campaign to reinstate Huang as CEO of Nvidia
item.description: Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'It's close to bulletproof' doctor says of MMR vaccine as measles cases rise
item.description: Global health authorities are expected to announce that the U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health milestone it achieved 26 years ago. This past year, the number of cases in the U.S. doubled, making it the worst year in three decades. That was the focus of the latest episode of Horizons with William Brangham.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Understaffing and unexpected fire behavior led to firefighter deaths, investigation finds
item.description: Unexpected fire behavior, chronic understaffing, a lack of highly trained employees and a new policy to quash fires quickly were among the factors that contributed to the deaths of four helitack firefighters as they battled a blaze in western Colorado in June, according to a report released by the U.S. Department of the Interior.

item.title: NPR: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
item.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: 'You never notice broken windows, obviously,' Trump tells Black reporter
item.description: President Donald Trump berated NBC News White House correspondent Yamiche Alcindor on Monday after she asked him to respond to critics who say he was too focused on construction projects in the nation's capital instead of issues with the country's airline systems, which came to a halt Friday in a rare nationwide FAA ground stop.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Read the full White House memo requiring agencies to get approval before testifying in front of Congress
item.description: In a new memorandum obtained by PBS News on Monday, White House counsel Will Scharf is directing all federal agencies and executive departments to get approval from White House legal and legislative affairs offices before agreeing to testify before congressional committees.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Customers at major banks are experiencing issues accessing their accounts
item.description: Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some major banks Monday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Freeman Johnson, the oldest of the dwindling number of Pearl Harbor survivors, dies at 106
item.description: Freeman Johnson was below deck working on a boiler of the USS St. Louis when the Japanese attack happened in December 1941.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Third U.S. aircraft carrier in Middle East as Trump keeps options open in Iran war
item.description: A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East. A U.S. official speaking on the condition of anonymity on Monday confirmed the USS Theodore Roosevelt's arrival in the region.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI tech
item.description: The Trump administration has issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers.

item.title: NPR: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Raye leads 2027 Grammy nominations as women dominate top categories
item.description: The Recording Academy announced the 2027 Grammy Award nominations on Monday, with English singer-songwriter Raye leading the pack.

item.title: NPR: Regulating AI will being a top priority for congressional Democrats in the new year
item.description: A big priority for the incoming Congress will be regulating artificial intelligence. Democrats will face stiff opposition from the Trump administration and its hands-off policy towards AI.

item.title: NPR: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
item.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The Nvidia scandal is heightening America's AI rivalry with China ahead of Trump's visit
item.description: Well before reports emerged that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, the advanced chips made by his company were at the center of the race between the U.S. and China to dominate artificial intelligence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Preliminary study finds a clue in the quest to help diagnose CTE in the living
item.description: Scientists stumbled onto a hint that measuring a toxic protein tied to Alzheimer's disease just might one day be useful in diagnosing a different brain disease in football players and others who have suffered repeated blows to the head.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion
item.description: A coalition of countries seeking to accelerate the global transition away from fossil fuels is preparing to unveil new national plans at the ongoing United Nations climate talks, known as COP31, in Antalya, Turkey, pressing ahead despite the withdrawal of Colombia, one of its founding members.

item.title: NPR: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
item.description: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: EU accuses Russia of stalling Ukraine peace talks to target power plants as winter nears
item.description: European Union countries on Monday accused Russia of trying to drag out talks on ending the war in Ukraine while it bombs power plants and other infrastructure to make life even harder for civilians as winter closes in.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russia says its defenses intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack
item.description: Russia intercepted 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine, Russia's Defense Ministry said Monday, in what was the most claimed downings since Moscow's all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: At least 17 people killed in 2 mass shootings on the same day in South Africa
item.description: At least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on the same day in South Africa. Motives have not been immediately established for the crimes some 530 kilometers (330 miles) apart, police said Monday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of strikes that killed 3 including a child, and other Mideast news
item.description: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels blamed Saudi Arabia on Monday for two strikes that killed three people in Houthi-controlled Yemen. The Saudi government did not immediately comment.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's Asia reset: Deals in Manila and Shenzhen, then a rare nuclear summit with Xi and Putin
item.description: President Donald Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington.

item.title: NPR: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
item.description: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

item.title: NPR: Affordability was a key issue for midterm voters. It helped make childcare one, too
item.description: Childcare costs have surged, putting a major financial burden on U.S. families. Advocates say the subject once on the fringes of political debate became a major issue during the midterms.

item.title: NPR: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
item.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

item.title: NPR: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The trip to China marks Trump's second time this year, and comes as the president and his party faced widespread backlash from voters in the recent midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Democratic strategists think Montana House race could hold the secret to future wins
item.description: Montana is sending a Democrat to the U.S. House for the first time in three decades. Many in the party think Sam Forstag's campaign may be a playbook for how Democrats can win again in rural America

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Officials say a tanker's steering failed before it crashed into a cruise ship in New Orleans
item.description: The preliminary finding from National Transportation Safety Board officials provided the first official word on what caused Friday's crash of the Atlantic Asphalt tanker into the American Heritage cruise ship, which sent passengers, crew and two police officers plunging into the Mississippi River.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's handpicked party chair faces a rebellion as midterm losses challenge president's grip on GOP
item.description: The emerging fight, which will shape the 2028 presidential nominating contest, represents a rare challenge to Trump's dominance, even after the party's worst midterm performance in a generation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 2 planes collide on the ground in Miami, only minor injuries reported
item.description: The accident happened at about 9 p.m. Saturday and involved a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 aircraft with 172 people aboard and a UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane, according to the National Transportation Safety Board and Copa Airlines.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Southeast Asian leaders open annual summit with major conflicts and their impact topping the agenda
item.description: The ASEAN leaders are likely to renew calls for self-restraint and peaceful resolutions of conflicts, including longstanding disputes in the South China Sea and a civil war in Myanmar.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo 6 months into response
item.description: More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope crosses Peru in the finale of a trip home to visit flock high in Andes and deep in Amazon
item.description: On the penultimate day of his visit to his adopted homeland, Leo channeled Pope Francis by emphasizing Catholic teaching that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God's creation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Zelenskyy says Starshield restrictions threaten Ukraine's energy defenses ahead of winter
item.description: Restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield satellite communications system are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump blasts judge's 2-week halt to his Washington golf project and says administration will appeal
item.description: "It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court," said Trump, who spent much of the weekend posting photos on his social media site of the golf course. "They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!"

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Could everything be broken? Grounded jets, Microsoft outage, AI chaos make some wonder
item.description: Throw in a few more examples just from Friday — a cruise ship that overturned in New Orleans when a tanker slammed into it, suspicious drones over a U.S. air base in Britain, a bomb found near an ethanol plant in Ohio.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 as company conducts internal probe over Nvidia fallout
item.description: Megaspeed, which is under scrutiny over alleged transfers of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies, also announced an internal investigation led by outside lawyers.

item.title: NPR: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a fine line with Trump
item.description: A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump breaks silence on nationwide ground stop and demands more money from Congress
item.description: The president has been conspicuously quiet on the ground stop since it began Friday afternoon, instead issuing statements on social media about completely different topics as frustrated passengers were left stranded at airports and his government scrambled with airlines to restore normal travel.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on D.C. public golf course redevelopment
item.description: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the temporary restraining order before the East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.

item.title: NPR: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a thin line with Trump
item.description: A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

item.title: NPR: Politics chat: Duffy calls for more funding, Democrats plans for accountability
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.

item.title: NPR: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
item.description: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

item.title: NPR: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
item.description: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

item.title: NPR: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on Washington public golf course redevelopment
item.description: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

item.title: NPR: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
item.description: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why a problem on the ground can affect flights thousands of miles away among other issues
item.description: Michael McCormick, a former airspace manager with the Federal Aviation Administration, said it could take days for airlines — many of which had to divert flights — to resume normal operations after officials lifted the grounding order.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: SpaceX's Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
item.description: It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday's liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: With shifting Iran rhetoric following U.S. elections, Trump leaves Middle East in limbo about path ahead
item.description: Trump's tonal shifts have only added to the uncertainty about what comes next in a war in which America's allies were not consulted before it was started but nonetheless struggle to deal with its economic ramifications.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The U.S. flu season is off to a very early start. It's hitting the South and West now
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday posted its latest update, reporting that seven states were reporting high flu activity last week, up from two states the week before.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Zelenskyy says a new European security framework floated by U.S. could benefit Putin
item.description: European leaders have stressed that decisions about the continent's security must be made by Europeans themselves, warning against allowing Russia to dictate the terms of a new security order or negotiate NATO's future.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New Orleans port sues to get control of tanker that crashed into cruise ship on Mississippi River
item.description: The lawsuit, filed by the Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans, said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker caused at least $1 million in damage to its terminal. A judge issued a warrant Friday giving federal officials control of the ship for now.

item.title: NPR: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
item.description: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Alaska voters reject ballot measure seeking to repeal open primaries and ranked voting system
item.description: The ballot measure, decided as part of the Nov. 3 election, marked the second time in two years that voters have rejected attempts to overturn the system and revert to partisan primaries and to general elections in which just one candidate can be selected.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about flights after the U.S. nationwide ground stop
item.description: The longest flight stoppage in 25 years ended around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, allowing some domestic flights to take off from U.S. airports. Officials expected a full recovery by Sunday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats try out a strange new emotion at post-midterms What's Next conference: hope
item.description: Democrats spent two days chewing over their future at the What's Next conference and trying to deal with the fact that it looks, for a moment at least, quite bright.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. gives states another 6 months before they have to remove people from Medicaid for not working
item.description: The administration clarified that while states still have the option to take action at the beginning of the year, they won't have to kick anyone off or deny coverage for failure to meet the requirement until July 1.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Rubio delivers keynote address at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention
item.description: Rubio gave a sweeping speech to fellow conservatives on Friday evening acknowledging that Americans are struggling in the current economy, while also railing against what he called the "weaponization" of international law to constrain the U.S. from acting in its own interests.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins becomes first Democrat since 1998 elected governor in Alaska
item.description: His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
item.description: The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hourslong episode had impacted some of their operations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Thousands of flights canceled as airlines work to recover from nationwide ground stop
item.description: The nationwide stop was the first since January 2023, when another key Federal Aviation Administration computer system that sends notices to pilots malfunctioned, and the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

item.title: NPR: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
item.description: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
item.description: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
item.description: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.

item.title: NPR: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over plan to sell public lands to states and tribes
item.description: The Trump administration wants to sell some federal public lands to states, local governments and tribes, a plan that's once again drawing swift bi-partisan opposition.

item.title: NPR: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
item.description: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.

item.title: NPR: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
item.description: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.

item.title: NPR: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
item.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
item.description: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Tanker crashes into river cruise boat in New Orleans
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, a ship collided with a river cruise boat in New Orleans, causing it to sink in the Mississippi River, some Microsoft users were offline for a second day as the company scrambled to restore its widely used suite of workplace software and the White House is tightening rules on how staffers interact with lobbyists.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bessent accuses Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia chips
item.description: The fallout of Jensen Huang's downfall expanded into a public fight between two of President Trump's top advisers. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia's most advanced chips. Nick Schifrin looks at the finger-pointing and the ongoing efforts to control advanced technology exports to China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Increasing cost of housing squeezes Americans out of market
item.description: Sales of existing homes in the U.S. fell last month to their lowest level in more than 16 years. That's according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. In October alone, sales dropped to 3.75 million homes, an 8.8% drop compared with the same time last year. Stephanie Sy reports on what's driving the decline.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Does Van Hollen have enough support to beat Schumer in Senate leadership race?
item.description: Senate Democrats won back their majority last week, and now they're fighting over who will lead it. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen has thrown his hat in the ring and says he will take on current Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports on the first serious challenge Schumer has faced to his party leadership.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: ICE touts record number of deportations in agency's history
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security reports that immigrant deportations and arrests hit an all-time high. More than 491,000 people were arrested by ICE in the last fiscal year, and more than 483,000 were deported. The Trump administration has said it aims to deport one million immigrants annually. William Brangham discussed more with John Sandweg, who was acting ICE Director under President Obama.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about Microsoft's outage and why it takes so long to restore email services
item.description: Unlike modern web apps or authentication gatekeepers, email wasn't designed to fail fast, meaning to immediately halt when a problem arises.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Marcus on how Republicans are responding to midterm losses
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Ruth Marcus of The New Yorker join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and what the Trump administration knew, how Republicans are responding to their losses in the midterm elections, JD Vance's chances in 2028 and the Democratic leadership battle in the Senate.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Celebrated countertenor brings classical sound to today's cultural issues
item.description: Anthony Roth Costanzo cuts an unusual figure in the world of music. The leading international opera singer is performing in the Metropolitan Opera's critically acclaimed and wildly popular "Lincoln at the Bardo," which the Met will stream for free to the public on Saturday. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown has the story for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: NPR: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin says FAA flight stoppage 'isn't another 9/11'
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there are no indications of an attack against the nation, after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon due to communications problems.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. wrongly withheld New York highway funds over immigrant licenses, appeals court rules
item.description: The U.S. Transportation Department wrongly decided to withhold nearly $74 million in highway money from New York state after it refused to revoke nearly 33,000 questionable commercial driver's licenses for immigrants when an audit revealed problems last year, a federal appeals court said Friday.

item.title: NPR: DHS head Mark Waye Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Waye Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

item.title: NPR: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
item.description: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

item.title: NPR: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FAA grounds all flights at U.S. airports due to air traffic control communications problems
item.description: The FAA notice said the ground stop was being imposed "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado loses U.S. House seat to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
item.description: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Rep. Lauren Boebert for a Colorado U.S. House seat on Friday, ousting a three-term Republican and staple of conservative media.

item.title: NPR: Latino voters help fuel Kansas' blue wave
item.description: In southwest Kansas, three majority-Latino counties shocked the political establishment by going blue for the first time in decades. Voters and activists say immigration enforcement was a big factor.

item.title: NPR: DEM SENATE LEADER FIGHT
item.description: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.
